constants.$comment: The engine exports RATE_BASES (200000, 1000000, 100000000) and no other constant a course could grade. Digest section 1 prints them from the export and section 3 checks 100 x 40 x 50 against OSHA_200K. The Lanczos coefficients and the iteration tolerances are implementation, not teaching, and are never graded.

plan.state: FOUNDATION COMPLETE. Engine vendored at f123a57, digest built (28 sections), fields.json and precision.json generated from the one tolerance derivation, 18 graded fields discriminating, lab and three panels shipped with vitest. No lesson, bank, key truth or migration is written yet.
plan.thesis: A safety rate is a count divided by exposure hours on a base somebody chose. Associate owns WHAT IS THE RATE, Professional owns HOW SURE ARE WE, Expert owns IS ANYTHING CHANGING. Each capstone grades only its own tier's question.

tiers.beginner: Associate: rates and bases. m01 a rate is a count over exposure (hours not headcount, the base required, the refusals), m02 TRIR DART LTIR on two bases, m03 FAR severity rate PSE rate, m04 sum then divide, m05 the rolling rate, m06 one report end to end. Digest sections 1 to 12.
tiers.intermediate: Professional: uncertainty. m01 the Poisson count model, m02 the Garwood interval, m03 zero events and the rule of three, m04 comparing two rates, m05 the central against the minlike p-value, m06 intervals in a report. Digest sections 13 to 20.
tiers.advanced: Expert: monitoring and judgement. m01 the u-chart, m02 signals, m03 what a signal means and revising limits, m04 benchmarking against IOGP published figures, m05 the traps (denominators, contractors, reclassification, rate chasing, the mean of rates one level up), m06 judgement end to end. Digest sections 21 to 27.

scopeSeams.the 5x5 risk matrix: OWNED BY riskchange (and EC6's 20/12/6 scale). This course never uses a risk matrix; a bare 'severity' here would collide with it, so the word is always 'severity rate'.
scopeSeams.FAR as a predicted rate: WILL BE OWNED BY H5 qra. H1 teaches an OBSERVED FAR only.
scopeSeams.percentile ranges: OWNED BY the economics uncertainty course and the Suite percentileConventions. A confidence interval here is on an estimated rate and carries no P label.

namingCollisions.Poisson: Poisson's ratio in geomech, rockphysics, porepressure, casingtubing, stimulation, perfsand. Always 'Poisson distribution' or 'Poisson count model'. Gated by gate_vocabulary.py.
namingCollisions.severity: a risk-matrix category (riskchange, compliance) and an exception level (surveillance). Always 'severity rate'. Gated.
namingCollisions.confidence interval: never a P10/P90 range; no P label anywhere. Gated.
namingCollisions.FAR: observed here, predicted in the planned H5. Reported for a human read by gate_vocabulary.py.

openItems.FINDINGS rationale sentence: FINDINGS-safetystats.md judgement call 4 says the upper limit is solved on the upper tail 'because 1 - 0.025 is not exactly 0.975 in floating point'. In IEEE double 1 - 0.025 === 0.975 is TRUE (digest section 16 asserts and prints it). The DESIGN is right for a different reason, which the digest measures: the lower-tail route loses digits as q shrinks and at q = 1e-17 cannot be asked at all. Provenance wording only; no engine number moves. Belongs in a petrolord-engines docs PR, not in the vendored copy.
openItems.missing-base message on pseRate: pseRate's missing-base refusal is the shared checkBase message, which offers 100,000,000 for FAR as a choice; pseRate then refuses that base. A learner who follows the message is refused a second time. UX only; worth one line in the engines repo.
openItems.benchmark data: The engine carries no IOGP benchmark table; Expert m04 benchmarks against the IOGP figures in the vendored golden only.
